body:
Owner: seen, and agreed — the current "Represent a recall" blurb lists the graph's contents and never says how a sentence becomes those pieces. Draft for the docs-site editor. Suggested home: a short linked page, How a transcript becomes a recall graph, from the Represent a recall heading. Not landed here; docs-site remains unclaimed.

Take the guide's own line:

One of the men with him got hit by an arrow and they lifted him into the boat.

RecallSegmenter.segment is a deterministic baseline, not a theory of memory. Same input always yields the same graph. A later parser or model can replace the heuristics; the checked RecallGraph is the contract that stays.

It does five things, in order.

1. It reads the transcript as surface text. Sentences and their character offsets are recorded first, so every later claim can point at exact words.

2. It splits sentences into idea units at connectives. Semicolons, "and then", "then", "but", "so", "because", "while", "before that" / "after that", and "and" followed by a new subject (he, she, they, the, a, ...) start a new unit. Short fragments stay attached so "and then" does not mint a one-word unit. On the example, "and they" is that last rule: two units, not one.

   - One of the men with him got hit by an arrow
   - they lifted him into the boat

3. It names who was mentioned and which mentions are the same person. "the men", "him", "they", "him" become recalled entities plus coreference links. The second "him" is the man who was hit, not a new stranger. This is a shallow, rule-based guess, and the graph records it as such.

4. It labels each unit. Hedging ("I think", "maybe") is marked when it is the speaker's, not quoted speech. Discourse function says what the unit is doing: telling an episode, evaluating, inferring, associating, commenting on the task, or saying the speaker cannot remember. The example is two episodic assertions — the speaker is reporting what happened, not judging the story.

5. It records explicit temporal and causal edges only where a connective licenses them. "because" can support cause; "then" / "and then" can support sequence. Precedence is not treated as causation. A bare "and they" does not mint a causal law.

RecallGraph.validated then checks the pieces fit: units stay inside the transcript, relations name units that exist, entities are consistent. The Checked phantom is that proof. If the pieces do not fit, the segmenter refuses the graph rather than publishing a broken one.

What this page should not imply: that the library has understood the story, or that these units are the scientifically correct idea units. They are a reproducible first cut so alignment has something honest to match against. The science lives in the alignment and the uncertainty that follows, not in the splitter.

If the editor wants this shorter on the getting-started page, keep the two-unit walk-through and one sentence that the rest is a baseline; put the five steps on the linked page.
